title: Tuple Technologies at DAC 2026 - Semiwiki
gist: Daniel Payne's DAC 2026 writeup of Tuple Technologies: a 45-person New Jersey company selling Stratos, an infrastructure-as-code subscription that stands up cloud EDA environments in 20 minutes instead of the three months a dedicated IT/CAD team would need, plus Nitro license analytics claiming up to 25% software cost cuts and Avestra, an 8-agent SystemVerilog Assertion generator positioned against roughly 30% hallucination rates from using Claude alone.

themes.theme: Cloud EDA infrastructure as a subscription

insights.claim: Tuple Technologies, founded in 2017 and now about 45 people headquartered in New Jersey, sells IT infrastructure for IC design teams as a subscription platform called Stratos rather than as consulting.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: A sub-50-person vendor attacking cloud EDA infrastructure signals the layer is still unowned by Cadence, Synopsys or the hyperscalers.
insights.quote: Tuple was founded in 2017 and has grown to about 45 people, headquartered in New Jersey.
insights.locator: At #DAC2026 I met with Vamshi Kothur

insights.claim: The core pitch is time compression: a specialized IT and CAD team would take three months to build an equivalent cloud EDA setup, while Tuple claims it is done in 20 minutes or less.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: If the 3-months-to-20-minutes delta holds, chip startups can defer hiring IT/CAD headcount entirely — lowering the fixed cost of founding a silicon company.
insights.quote: A specialized IT & CAD teams would take 3 months to do a similar setup, but now it’s done in 20 minutes.
insights.locator: A software-based service enables design version control

insights.claim: AWS, Google and Azure each differ enough to create a learning curve for IT and CAD teams, which is the friction Tuple monetizes by abstracting cloud choice away from the design team.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: Hyperscaler heterogeneity is a durable moat for abstraction-layer vendors; it also caps any single cloud's ability to lock in EDA workloads.
insights.quote: Cloud providers AWS, Google and Azure are each slightly different and create a learning curve for IT & CAD teams to master.
insights.locator: Cloud providers AWS, Google and Azure

insights.claim: Treating design infrastructure as Infrastructure As Code gives version control over system configuration, so teams can roll back configuration drift and recover fast from disasters — one customer recovered from a ransomware attack by rolling back to a clean state.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: Ransomware resilience is becoming a purchasing criterion in chip design IT — a security angle that sells infrastructure software into engineering budgets.
insights.quote: One customer encountered a Ransomware attack, but they could just roll back in time to have a clean start.
insights.locator: A software-based service enables design version control

themes.theme: Cost control: licenses, spot compute, multi-cloud

insights.claim: Tuple's Nitro license monitor integrates EDA license tracking with job schedulers and claims to cut engineering software costs by up to 25% through data-driven renewal decisions.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: A credible 25% cut in EDA license spend is a direct headwind to seat-count growth at Cadence, Synopsys and Siemens if utilization analytics spread.
insights.quote: cutting engineering software costs by up to 25% by using data-driven renewal decisions
insights.locator: Financial types will love the Billing tracker app

insights.claim: Tuple's Omni orchestrates across multiple clouds so that when GPU needs exceed a hyperscaler allocation, workloads can be checked out to another hyperscaler or a neocloud at lower cost.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: Orchestration layers that arbitrage GPU scarcity across neoclouds erode hyperscaler pricing power at the margin — watch for the pattern beyond EDA.
insights.quote: Omni can check out other Hyperscaler or Neo cloud to provide you with availability with lower costs
insights.locator: Omni is used for multi-cloud orchestration

insights.claim: Running EDA jobs on spot instances — excess hyperscaler compute — can improve turnaround time at lower cost, as demonstrated with Cadence Pegasus on the cloud at a Cadence Live presentation.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: Spot-priced verification and physical-verification runs change the cost curve for tapeouts; interruption-tolerant EDA flows become a competitive advantage.
insights.locator: You can even use Spot instances

insights.claim: Budget allocation can be set and tracked with alerts across users, teams, projects and departments, so cloud and tool costs stop being a guess for the duration of a project.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: FinOps discipline arriving in chip design suggests cloud EDA is moving from experiment to budgeted line item.
insights.locator: Financial types will love the Billing tracker app

insights.claim: Funded startups routinely hit the problem that they cannot run Calibre inside a Cadence chamber; Tuple's answer is allowing Cadence and Siemens tools on the same network so teams can mix and match tools from multiple EDA and IP vendors.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: Vendor-lock friction at the infrastructure layer is a real constraint on best-of-breed tool buying; removing it favors point-tool leaders like Siemens Calibre.
insights.quote: Startups can get funded, then buy some EDA tools, but they cannot use Calibre inside of a Cadence chamber.

insights.claim: TroposAlerts provides incident management and escalation for broken infrastructure or bad RTL check-ins, paging, texting or emailing responsible engineers and escalating up the chain if nobody responds.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: Chip design IT is adopting software-industry on-call patterns; PagerDuty-style tooling is being rebuilt vertically for silicon teams.
insights.locator: What about the case where in the middle of the night

insights.claim: Using Claude directly for SystemVerilog Assertion generation comes with roughly 30% hallucinations producing incorrect results, according to Tuple's Ashok Mehta.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: A concrete hallucination rate is the yardstick for whether general LLMs or purpose-built agent pipelines win in verification — the gap is the startups' entire value proposition.
insights.quote: Claude can be used for SVA generation, however you must live with 30% hallucinations giving incorrect results.
insights.locator: Ashok Mehta from Tuple Tech talked about

insights.claim: Avestra is an 8-agent pipeline trained to eliminate incorrect assertions caused by tautology, using a proprietary RAG database plus domain expertise from Ashok Mehta's 22 patents and three books.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: The defensible layer in AI-EDA is domain-specific correctness checking and proprietary retrieval data, not the underlying model.
insights.quote: Avestra is an 8-agent pipeline that has been trained to eliminate incorrect assertions caused by tautology.
insights.locator: Ashok Mehta from Tuple Tech talked about

insights.claim: Avestra generates assertions from natural-language specs and RTL for Questa, VCS and Xcelium, cross-checks spec against RTL to find inconsistencies, suggests fixes, and generates a coverage-driven test bench.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: Simulator-agnostic AI verification tools ride on top of all three big EDA vendors rather than competing with them — an attach-rate business model.
insights.locator: Ashok Mehta from Tuple Tech talked about

insights.claim: Initial Avestra users include a big foundry and a memory design company, indicating early traction with production silicon teams rather than only startups.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: Anonymous tier-1 references are the early signal to track before public logos appear; foundry and memory adoption implies the tools survive high-rigor flows.
insights.quote: Initial users of Avestra include a big foundry and a memory design company.
insights.locator: When using Avestra you can triage

insights.claim: Smaller EDA vendors take more risks with new technology and often reap more rewards than their larger competitors, a pattern the author says holds for Tuple in 2026.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: Useful screen for where AI-EDA innovation shows up first: small private vendors, which then become acquisition targets for the big three.
insights.quote: Smaller EDA vendors take more risks and often reap more rewards than their larger competitors with new technology
